From .qmd to published article

How every article on this site comes about: write in RStudio, render, push to GitHub, Netlify publishes.

workflow
Quarto
Author

Edward F. Hillenaar

Published

January 19, 2026

On this page

  • Four steps
  • Why rendered HTML is committed
  • Draft and publication

Four steps

  1. Write. New article: en/posts/YYYY-MM-DD-slug/index.qmd. The YAML header carries title, description, date, categories and image. The prose is markdown; calculations sit in R chunks.
  2. Render. In RStudio: Build → Render Website, or quarto render in the terminal. The result lands in _site/, including the figures the R chunks drew.
  3. Push. Source and _site/ go to GitHub in one commit.
  4. Publish. Netlify picks up _site and puts the new version live. No build step on the server.

Why rendered HTML is committed

Because the R chunks need packages and data that need not live on a build server. Rendering locally keeps output reproducible on one machine and the deploy simple: Netlify publishes what is there.

freeze: auto in _quarto.yml makes a chunk re-run only when its .qmd file changed. The stored results live in _freeze/ and are committed too.

Draft and publication

Set draft: true in the YAML header and the article stays out of the listing. Half-finished pieces sit safely in the repository without going live.

---
title: "Working title"
date: 2026-09-01
draft: true
---

## Four steps

1. **Write.** New article: `en/posts/YYYY-MM-DD-slug/index.qmd`. The YAML header
   carries title, `description`, `date`, `categories` and `image`. The prose is
   markdown; calculations sit in R chunks.
2. **Render.** In RStudio: **Build → Render Website**, or `quarto render` in the
   terminal. The result lands in `_site/`, including the figures the R chunks drew.
3. **Push.** Source and `_site/` go to GitHub in one commit.
4. **Publish.** Netlify picks up `_site` and puts the new version live. No build
   step on the server.

## Why rendered HTML is committed

Because the R chunks need packages and data that need not live on a build
server. Rendering locally keeps output reproducible on one machine and the deploy
simple: Netlify publishes what is there.

`freeze: auto` in `_quarto.yml` makes a chunk re-run only when its `.qmd` file
changed. The stored results live in `_freeze/` and are committed too.

## Draft and publication

Set `draft: true` in the YAML header and the article stays out of the listing.
Half-finished pieces sit safely in the repository without going live.

```yaml
---
title: "Working title"
date: 2026-09-01
draft: true
---
```
